mainTopic: Trumpet blasts in the מקדש: the 48-blast limit, the fixed calendar, and the songs of ראש חודש on שבת
overview: The גמרא first looks for a second 48-blast day that the משנה left out. It rejects weekday ערב הפסח, which comes to only 42 by רבי יהודה's view, and settles on ערב הפסח that falls on Friday. It then quotes the משנה's rule that no day has more than 48 blasts. It challenges that rule with ערב הפסח on שבת, which has 51 or 57 blasts, and answers that the תנא lists only cases that happen every year. A Friday inside סוכות is shown to happen every year, because the calendar is pushed off so that יום הכפורים never falls next to שבת. Sources that let יום הכפורים fall next to שבת are explained as following אחרים, who hold a fixed calendar, while our משנה follows רבנן. Finally the גמרא tests רבי אחא בר חנינא's view of separate blasts for each מוסף, using the songs for ראש חודש that falls on שבת. That leads to רב ספרא's reading and רבי יוחנן's reason, and ends with a challenge that another sign for ראש חודש already exists. That challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Weekday Passover eve does not reach 48
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion that the תנא left out ערב הפסח is rejected. The משנה follows רבי יהודה, so on that day the third group gets only 3 blasts and the total is 42, not 48.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the omitted case is ערב הפסח, that is not really an omission. The author of this משנה is רבי יהודה, who said: in all its days, the third group never reached the words 'I love that God hears,' because its people were few.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the earlier answer that the תנא left out ערב הפסח. That day does not reach 48 according to the opinion this משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ערב הפסח the קרבן פסח was slaughtered in three groups. For each reading of הלל, 3 blasts were sounded, and הלל was normally read up to three times per group, giving 9 blasts per group. רבי יהודה says the third group was so small that it never even reached the second paragraph of הלל, so it had only 3 blasts. The total is then 21 + 9 + 9 + 3 = 42, so this is not a 48-blast day the תנא forgot to mention.

keyTerms.meaning: an omission, something the תנא left out of a list
the day before פסח, when the קרבן פסח was slaughtered
the third group of people bringing the קרבן פסח
'who is it?', asking which תנא is the author
few in number

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the third group skipped הלל. They began it, but finished slaughtering before reaching 'אהבתי', so only one set of blasts was sounded for them.

phrases.english: If it is because of Passover eve —
that is not an omission,
for who is the author? It is Rabbi Yehuda,
who said: never in all the days of the third group
did it reach the point of saying
'I love that the Lord hears',
phrases.notes: תהלים 116:1, the second paragraph of הלל

phrases.english: because its people were few.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִשּׁוּם עֶרֶב הַפֶּסַח — לָאו שִׁיּוּרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer on the previous amud, which said the תנא omitted ערב הפסח.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects weekday ערב הפסח as a 48-blast case the תנא left out.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: According to רבי יהודה, the author of the משנה, that day has only 42 blasts.

steps.title: But the משנה was shown not to follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that it already established earlier that this משנה does not follow רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we already established that the משנה is not like רבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the previous step. Earlier in the sugya it proved that this משנה disagrees with רבי יהודה, so how can it now rely on his view?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 only works if the author of the משנה is רבי יהודה. But an earlier part of the sugya, about how the blasts are counted, showed the משנה goes against רבי יהודה. That seems to knock out the basis of the rejection.

keyTerms.meaning: we established; we set the משנה as following a certain view
not in accordance with

phrases.english: But didn't we establish
that it is not like Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אוֹקֵימְנָא דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the assumption in step 1 that רבי יהודה is the author.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 1 that the משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It contradicts the earlier conclusion that the משנה does not follow רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The תנא agrees on one point and disagrees on another
steps.stepSummary: The תנא can follow רבי יהודה about the third group, while still disagreeing with him about how the blasts are counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps this תנא agrees with him in one matter and disagrees with him in another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. A תנא does not have to agree or disagree with רבי יהודה on everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא accepts רבי יהודה's report that the third group never reached 'אהבתי'. But he disagrees with רבי יהודה on the separate counting question discussed earlier. So the rejection in step 1 stands, and weekday ערב הפסח is still only 42.

keyTerms.meaning: he holds like him
in one matter
he argues with him

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common move in the גמרא: one תנא may follow another תנא's view on one issue without following him on everything.

phrases.english: And perhaps this tanna
holds like him in one matter,
and disagrees with him in one matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא הַאי תַּנָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּווֹתֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2 and keeps the rejection of step 1 standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the issues: partial agreement with רבי יהודה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A תנא who disagrees with רבי יהודה must disagree with him on everything.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא follows רבי יהודה about the third group but not about the counting method.

steps.title: So what other case did the תנא omit?
steps.stepSummary: With ערב הפסח on a weekday ruled out, the גמרא repeats its question: which other 48-blast case did the תנא leave out?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: what else did he omit, that we can say he also omitted this one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its original question, setting up a new answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule behind 'מאי שייר דהאי שייר' is that a תנא does not leave out just one case; if he left out one, there must be another. Since ראש השנה on שבת is one omission and the first suggestion for a second one failed, the גמרא looks again, and the next step gives a new answer.

keyTerms.meaning: rather; we must look for another answer
what else did he leave out, that this one was also left out?

phrases.english: Rather: what did he omit, that he omitted this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: מַאי שַׁיַּיר דְּהַאי שַׁיַּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first suggestion was rejected, the original question returns.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Another day besides ראש השנה on שבת that reaches 48 blasts and is not listed in the משנה.

steps.title: Passover eve that falls on Friday
steps.stepSummary: The omitted case is ערב הפסח on ערב שבת. Six blasts are lost in the third group and six are added for ערב שבת, so the total comes back to 48.
steps.simpleTranslation: He omitted ערב הפסח that falls on ערב שבת: take out six, put in six.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to the question in step 4. This day really does reach exactly 48.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A full three-group count would be 21 + 27 = 48. By רבי יהודה's view, the third group loses 6 blasts (only 3 instead of 9). But on ערב שבת, 6 extra blasts are sounded to announce שבת. The 6 lost and the 6 added cancel out, so the total is 48.

keyTerms.meaning: Friday, the day before שבת
take out, subtract
bring in, add
six

steps.whatToRemember: Weekday ערב הפסח = 42 (by רבי יהודה). ערב הפסח on Friday = 48: minus 6 from the third group, plus 6 for ערב שבת.

phrases.english: He omitted Passover eve
that falls on Shabbat eve,
take out six and bring in six.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁיַּיר עֶרֶב הַפֶּסַח שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ערב הפסח on Friday: 6 blasts lost in the third group and 6 added for ערב שבת, totaling 48.

steps.title: משנה: never more than 48 blasts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the משנה: no more than 48 blasts are sounded on any day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one does not add beyond forty-eight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new phrase of the משנה. It is setting up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the גמרא asked which cases reach 48. Now it looks at the משנה's claim that 48 is the upper limit, which it will test against a case that seems to go higher.

keyTerms.meaning: one does not add (beyond)
forty-eight

phrases.english: And one does not add beyond forty-eight.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין מוֹסִיפִין עַל אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמֹנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the upper limit stated in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No more than 48 trumpet blasts are sounded in the מקדש on any day.

steps.title: Passover eve on שבת goes above 48
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the limit: ערב הפסח on שבת has 51 blasts according to רבי יהודה and 57 according to the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not more? But there is ערב הפסח that falls on שבת. According to רבי יהודה that makes fifty-one, and according to the רבנן fifty-seven!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the משנה's limit of 48 with a case that goes over it by either opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת there is a מוסף offering with 9 more blasts. רבי יהודה: 21 daily + 9 מוסף + 9 + 9 + 3 for the three groups = 51. רבנן, who give the third group a full 9: 21 + 9 + 27 = 57. Either way the total is above 48, so the משנה seems wrong. The next step answers this challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: and is it not so? (a challenging question)
but there is (a case)
fifty-one
fifty-seven
the Sages (the majority view)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up ערב הפסח on Friday (step 5, exactly 48) with ערב הפסח on שבת itself (here). On שבת there is a מוסף, which adds 9 blasts and pushes the total over 48.

phrases.english: And not?
But there is Passover eve
that falls on Shabbat,
where according to Rabbi Yehuda — fifty-one,
according to the Rabbis — fifty-seven!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא? וְהָא אִיכָּא עֶרֶב הַפֶּסַח שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה clause quoted in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that no day has more than 48 blasts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ערב הפסח on שבת adds the שבת מוסף blasts to the פסח blasts, giving 51 (רבי יהודה) or 57 (רבנן), both above 48.

steps.title: The תנא only lists cases that happen every year
steps.stepSummary: The 51/57-blast case of ערב הפסח on שבת is left out because it does not happen every year. The limit of 48 refers only to yearly cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the תנא teaches, he lists things that happen every year. ערב הפסח that falls on שבת does not happen every year, so he does not teach it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 7. ערב הפסח on שבת really has more than 48 blasts, but the משנה ignores it because it is not a yearly event.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule of 'no more than 48' is limited in scope. It only covers situations that come up every year. A rare calendar combination like ערב הפסח on שבת falls outside that list, so it does not contradict the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He (the תנא) teaches
Something that occurs every year
Which does not exist / does not occur

phrases.english: When he (the תנא) teaches,
he teaches something that occurs every year.
Passover eve that falls on Shabbat,
which does not occur each and every year,
he does not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָתָנֵי, מִידֵּי דְּאִיתֵיהּ בְּכׇל שָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the משנה's rule to yearly cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The limit of 48 applies to every possible day, including rare ones
steps.terutzMaskana: The limit of 48 applies only to days that occur every year, so ערב הפסח on שבת is excluded

steps.title: But a Friday inside סוכות is not yearly either
steps.stepSummary: The משנה itself counts ערב שבת שבתוך החג, yet some years there is no Friday inside the חג. This happens when the first day of סוכות falls on Friday.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say a Friday during the festival happens every year? Sometimes you won't find one. How so? For example, when the first day of יום טוב falls on Friday.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of Step 8. The משנה does list a case that is not yearly: a Friday during סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first day of סוכות (the 15th) is a Friday, then the next Friday (the 22nd) is שמיני עצרת, not part of the חג itself. So in that year there is no ערב שבת inside the חג. This breaks the rule that the משנה only lists yearly cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (a challenging opener)
A Friday during the festival of סוכות
Sometimes
And what is the case? / How so?

phrases.english: Is that to say that a Friday within the festival
occurs every year?
Sometimes you do not find it.
And what are the circumstances?

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁחָל יוֹם טוֹב רִאשׁוֹן בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: For example, when the first festival day falls on Friday.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת שֶׁבְּתוֹךְ הַחַג מִי אִיתֵיהּ בְּכׇל שָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה lists only yearly cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lists ערב שבת שבתוך החג, which is missing when the first day of סוכות falls on Friday

steps.title: The calendar never lets the first day of סוכות fall on Friday
steps.stepSummary: The calendar is pushed off so that the first day of סוכות never falls on Friday. Otherwise יום הכפורים would fall on Sunday, right after שבת. So there is always a Friday inside the חג.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the first day of יום טוב would fall on Friday, we push it off. Why? If the first day of the חג fell on Friday, when would יום הכפורים be? On Sunday. Therefore we push it off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends Step 8. The case raised in Step 9 never actually happens, because the calendar is arranged to prevent it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If סוכות began on Friday, ראש השנה would also be on Friday, and יום הכפורים would be on Sunday. To avoid having שבת and יום הכפורים back to back, the calendar is shifted. That means a Friday inside סוכות really does occur every year.

keyTerms.meaning: We definitely push it off (postpone it in the calendar)
What is the reason?
Sunday (the first day of the week)
Therefore

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not talking about moving סוכות by itself. The whole month is set in advance so that ראש השנה does not fall on certain days. That is why the first day of סוכות, which is two weeks later on the same weekday, never lands on Friday.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מִקְּלַע יוֹם טוֹב רִאשׁוֹן בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
phrases.english: When the first festival day happens to fall on Friday,
we postpone it.
What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאִיקְּלַע יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חַג
phrases.english: Since if the first festival day of the חג happened
to be on Friday,
when would יום הכפורים be?
On Sunday.
Therefore we postpone it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי מִקְּלַע יוֹם טוֹב רִאשׁוֹן בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת מִדְחֵי דָּחֵינַן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denying the case: the calendar prevents it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Some years have no Friday inside סוכות
steps.terutzMaskana: The calendar is set so that the first day of סוכות is never on Friday, so a Friday inside the חג exists every year
steps.whyThisMatters: This connects the counting of blasts to the rules of the fixed calendar. It is the basis of the well-known rule that יום הכפורים is not set next to שבת.

steps.title: A משנה assumes יום הכפורים can fall right after שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the calendar rule of Step 10. A משנה says that the fats of שבת offerings may be burned on יום הכפורים, which only makes sense if יום הכפורים can come right after שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really push it off? But we learned in a משנה: the fats of שבת offerings are offered on יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether the calendar is really pushed off to keep יום הכפורים away from שבת. It brings a משנה that pictures יום הכפורים falling on Sunday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'חלבי שבת' are fats of offerings brought on שבת that had not yet been burned on the altar. If they are burned on יום הכפורים, then יום הכפורים must be able to fall on Sunday, right after שבת. That contradicts Step 10's claim that we always prevent this.

keyTerms.meaning: And do we really...? (a challenging question)
But didn't we learn in a משנה?
Fats of offerings from שבת, still waiting to be burned on the altar
Are offered (burned on the altar)

phrases.english: And do we postpone it?
But didn't we learn in a משנה:
The fats of Shabbat offerings
are offered on Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי דָּחֵינַן לֵיהּ? וְהָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of Step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the calendar is pushed off so יום הכפורים never falls on Sunday
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה rules that שבת fats are burned on יום הכפורים, which assumes יום הכפורים can be on Sunday

steps.title: רבי זירא's report adds a ברייתא with יום הכפורים on Friday and on Sunday
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא reports a ברייתא that speaks of יום הכפורים falling on Friday and of יום הכפורים falling on Saturday night. In בבל they said everyone agrees with it. In ארץ ישראל, רבי יהודה son of רבי שמעון בן פזי said it follows only רבי עקיבא. Either way, some תנא holds that יום הכפורים can sit next to שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי זירא said: When we were in the study hall in בבל, they used to say that this ברייתא is everyone's opinion: when יום הכפורים fell on Friday, they did not blow the trumpets, and when it fell on Saturday night, they did not make הבדלה. When I went up to ארץ ישראל, I found רבי יהודה son of רבי שמעון בן פזי sitting and saying: It is the view of רבי עקיבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא strengthens the challenge of Step 11 with a second source. This ברייתא openly speaks of יום הכפורים falling both right before and right after שבת. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a Friday יום הכפורים, the blasts that normally tell people to stop working before שבת were not needed, since work was already forbidden. On a Saturday-night יום הכפורים, no הבדלה was said. The ברייתא assumes both calendar situations can happen. The only debate is whether all agree (the view in בבל) or only רבי עקיבא (the view in ארץ ישראל), but in both cases this goes against the 'pushing off' of Step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: The study hall of the rabbis
That which was taught in a ברייתא
Saturday night, after שבת ends
Recite הבדלה
Everyone's opinion; undisputed
I went up there (to ארץ ישראל)

steps.confusionAlert: The argument between בבל and ארץ ישראל is only about WHO holds this ברייתא. It does not weaken the challenge. Even if only רבי עקיבא holds it, there is still a תנא for whom יום הכפורים falls next to שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: The calendar answer of Step 10 is now under pressure from two sources, the משנה of חלבי שבת and the ברייתא of רבי זירא. Both assume יום הכפורים can fall next to שבת. The next step answers this by assigning the sources to different תנאים.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Zeira said:
When we were in the study hall in Babylonia,
they would say about that which was taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
phrases.english: Yom Kippur that falls on Friday,
they would not blow the trumpets,
and when it fell on Saturday night, they would not recite havdala
that it is everyone's opinion.
When I went up there (to Eretz Yisrael),

phrases.aramaic: אַשְׁכַּחְתֵּיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי,
phrases.english: I found Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi
sitting and saying:
It is the view of Rabbi Akiva!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: כִּי הֲוֵינַן בֵּי רַב בְּבָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source to the קשיא of Step 11
steps.raayaObject: That יום הכפורים can fall next to שבת, against the 'pushing off' of Step 10
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reported by רבי זירא, held by everyone (בבל) or by רבי עקיבא (ארץ ישראל)

steps.title: Each משנה follows a different תנא
steps.stepSummary: The contradiction from Step 11 is resolved. The משנה that always has a Friday inside the חג follows רבנן. The משנה about burning שבת fats on יום הכפורים follows אחרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one follows רבנן, and that one follows אחרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 11. It says the two משניות simply follow two different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן push off the calendar so that יום הכפורים never comes right after שבת. That is why our משנה can count on a Friday inside סוכות every year. אחרים do not push off the calendar at all. So for them יום הכפורים can fall on Sunday, and the fats of שבת offerings would be burned on יום הכפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; a standard opening for an answer
The Sages (the majority view)
'Others'; a תנא quoted under this title (often identified as רבי מאיר)

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: Our משנה, which assumes a Friday inside the חג every year.

phrases.english: that one is Aḥerim.
phrases.notes: The משנה about burning שבת fats on יום הכפורים.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא רַבָּנַן, הָא אֲחֵרִים הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 11 and backed up in Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Split the sources between two תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות seemed to follow one calendar system, so they contradicted each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה about Friday inside the חג follows רבנן, who push off the calendar. The משנה about שבת fats follows אחרים, who do not.

steps.title: The ברייתא of אחרים on a fixed-length year
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that according to אחרים, each holiday moves forward a fixed four days of the week from year to year (five in a leap year). So there is no pushing off, and ראש השנה can fall on any day.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: אחרים say, between שבועות and the next שבועות, and between ראש השנה and the next ראש השנה, there are only four days of difference. If it was a leap year, five.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for what it just said about אחרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular year of 354 days is 50 full weeks plus 4 days, so each holiday moves exactly 4 days forward in the week. A leap year moves it 5 days. Since אחרים say this never changes, nothing is ever pushed off. That means יום הכפורים can land on Sunday, right after שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
Here, the holiday of שבועות
A leap year, with an extra month

steps.confusionAlert: 'Four days' does not mean the holidays are four days apart. It means that next year the holiday falls four days later in the week. For example, Monday becomes Friday.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Aḥerim say:
there is nothing between Shavuot and Shavuot

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין בֵּין רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
phrases.english: and nothing between Rosh HaShana and Rosh HaShana
except four days of the week only,
phrases.notes: A 354-day year is 50 weeks plus 4 days.

phrases.english: and if it was a leap year — five.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the view of אחרים used in Step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That אחרים hold a fixed-length year with no pushing off of dates
steps.whatToRemember: רבנן push off ראש השנה, so יום הכפורים is never next to שבת. אחרים hold a fixed calendar, so it can be. This explains both משניות.

steps.title: Challenge from the songs of ראש חודש on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to רבי אחא בר חנינא's rule that each מוסף gets its own set of blasts. It challenges him from a ברייתא. When ראש חודש falls on שבת, the ראש חודש song 'pushes away' the שבת song, so it seems only one song is sung.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: When ראש חודש falls on שבת, the song of ראש חודש pushes away the song of שבת. But if רבי אחא is right, we should say the שבת song and also say the ראש חודש song!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the calendar topic. It returns to the question of blasts for each מוסף and brings a challenge from the songs sung in the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אחא בר חנינא holds that each מוסף gets its own blasts and, along with them, its own song. If so, on ראש חודש that falls on שבת, both songs should be sung. The ברייתא says one song 'pushes away' the other, which suggests only one song, and so only one set of blasts.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged, using a תנאי source
The song the לויים sang while an offering was brought
Pushes away, overrides
And if it were so (if that view were true)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
the New Moon that falls on Shabbat —
the song of the New Moon
pushes away the song of Shabbat.
And if it is so,
phrases.notes: That is, if רבי אחא בר חנינא is right that each מוסף gets its own blasts.

phrases.english: let us say that of Shabbat and say that of the New Moon!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the calendar side-discussion and goes back to the main question of blasts for each מוסף.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אחא בר חנינא's rule that each מוסף has its own blasts (and song)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If each מוסף had its own song, both songs would be sung. The ברייתא says one pushes the other away, which implies only one is sung.

steps.title: רב ספרא: 'Pushes away' means 'goes first'
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא explains that 'דוחה' does not mean the ראש חודש song cancels the שבת song. It means the ראש חודש song goes first, and both are sung.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said: What does 'pushes away' mean? It pushes ahead, to come first.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא defends רבי אחא בר חנינא by reading the word 'דוחה' differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that 'דוחה' means 'cancels'. רב ספרא reads it as 'takes the earlier place'. Both songs are sung, so the ברייתא fits the idea of separate blasts for each מוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the answer here
To go first, to come before

phrases.english: Rav Safra said:
what is 'pushes away'?
It pushes ahead to come first.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב סָפְרָא: מַאי דּוֹחֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15 by reinterpreting a key word.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'דוחה' means the ראש חודש song cancels the שבת song, so only one is sung.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'דוחה' means the ראש חודש song is sung first. Both songs are sung.

steps.title: Why should the less frequent song go first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב ספרא's reading. By the rule 'תדיר קודם', the more frequent שבת song should go first, not the ראש חודש song.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? When something frequent meets something not frequent, the frequent one comes first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב ספרא's answer. If 'דוחה' means 'goes first', that clashes with a known rule about which comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבת comes every week and ראש חודש comes only once a month, so שבת is the more frequent one. The rule 'תדיר ושאינו תדיר, תדיר קודם' says the more frequent practice goes first. So it makes no sense for the ראש חודש song to come before the שבת song.

keyTerms.meaning: And why?
Frequent, something that happens more often
The more frequent one goes first

phrases.english: And why?
frequent and not frequent —
the frequent one comes first!
phrases.notes: שבת (weekly) is more frequent than ראש חודש (monthly).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? תָּדִיר וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ תָּדִיר — תָּדִיר קוֹדֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ספרא's answer from Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ספרא's reading that the ראש חודש song goes first
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under the rule 'תדיר קודם', the weekly שבת song should come before the monthly ראש חודש song, so it cannot be that the ראש חודש song goes first.
steps.whyThisMatters: 'תדיר קודם' is a basic rule used throughout שס, for example in deciding which מצוה or offering comes first.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the ראש חודש song goes first to show the month was fixed on time
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains why the ראש חודש song goes first, even against the rule of תדיר קודם. It lets people know that ראש חודש was set on its proper day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: it is so that people will know that ראש חודש was fixed at its proper time.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question from Step 17. The ראש חודש song breaks the usual rule and goes first, as a public sign that ראש חודש was set on time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule תדיר קודם normally puts the more frequent thing (שבת) first. רבי יוחנן says there is a special reason to break that rule here. Putting ראש חודש first makes it stand out, so everyone hears that בית דין fixed the new month on the correct day.

keyTerms.meaning: To make known / so that people will know
Was fixed / was established (by בית דין)
At its proper time

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
To make known that Rosh Chodesh was established
phrases.notes: This explains why the ראש חודש song is sung first.

phrases.english: at its proper time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֵידַע שֶׁהוּקְבַּע רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ בִּזְמַנּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 17 (why ראש חודש goes before the more frequent שבת).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a special reason that overrides the general rule of תדיר קודם.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since שבת is more frequent, its song should be sung first.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ראש חודש song goes first on purpose, to publicize that ראש חודש was fixed on time.

steps.title: Challenge: there is already a different sign for this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether this is really the sign we use, since a different sign already exists to show that ראש חודש was fixed on time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this the sign we make? We already make a different sign!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן. It says we already have another sign showing that ראש חודש was set on time, and the next step quotes the source for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a sign for ראש חודש already exists, why would we need a second one through the order of the songs? That makes רבי יוחנן's reason look unnecessary. This step only makes the claim; the proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A sign / a marker that makes something recognizable
We make / we do
Another / a different one

phrases.english: And is this the sign that we make?
But we make a different sign!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַאי הֶיכֵּירָא עָבְדִינַן? הָא הֶיכֵּירָא אַחֲרִינָא עָבְדִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's answer in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reason that the ראש חודש song goes first as a sign.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A separate sign for ראש חודש already exists, so this one seems unneeded.

steps.title: The source: ראש חודש fats were placed in their own special spot
steps.stepSummary: A taught source says the fats of each kind of offering were placed in a different spot. The fats of the ראש חודש offerings had their own spot, beneath the ledge of the altar. That is the 'other sign.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: the fats of the morning תמיד were placed from the middle of the ramp and down, on the east side. The fats of the מוספין were placed from the middle of the ramp and down, on the west side. The fats of ראש חודש were placed under the ledge of the altar and below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source behind its challenge. Because the ראש חודש fats had their own special place, that already served as a sign for ראש חודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each group of fats was set down in a separate place before going onto the altar, so they would not get mixed up. The ראש חודש fats were given a unique spot of their own. The גמרא treats this as the existing ראש חודש sign, which is why רבי יוחנן's song-order sign seems extra.

keyTerms.meaning: The fats (of the offerings), which are burned on the altar
The daily morning offering
The ramp leading up to the altar
The additional offerings (of שבת and holidays)
The ledge that goes around the altar

steps.confusionAlert: The fats were not burned at these spots. They were only set down there for a while before being brought up to the altar. Each group had its own spot so the groups stayed separate.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
The fats of the daily morning offering
are placed from the middle of the ramp and below, on the east side,
and those of the additional offerings are placed
from the middle of the ramp and below, on the west side,
and those of Rosh Chodesh are placed
under the ledge of the altar and below.
phrases.notes: This unique spot is the 'other sign' for ראש חודש.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא חֶלְבֵי תָּמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the challenge made in Step 19.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a separate sign for ראש חודש already exists.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A taught source (דתניא) about where the fats of the different offerings were placed: the ראש חודש fats went under the altar's ledge.
